title: Officer cleared in shooting of youth
article: An out-of-province review has cleared a Winnipeg police officer who shot and killed an aboriginal youth who refused to drop a screwdriver, police and legal sources said Wednesday.
The report into the Jan. 31, 2005 fatal shooting of Matthew Dumas has recommended no charges against the police officer involved.
The review by an Ontario Crown attorney was only sent to Manitoba justice officials earlier in the week and has not been discussed at length with the officer involved or the Dumas family.
Its arrival ends a more than two-year legal odyssey in which police officials sought independent opinions on whether their own probe into Dumas' death was complete.
Police have said officers pursued Dumas as a suspect in an Elmwood home invasion, first down a back lane and then onto the front street of Dufferin Avenue, about two blocks west of Salter Street.
Dumas scuffled with an officer in a lane, broke free and darted between two houses onto Dufferin where he was met by other officers.

Police have said he had a screwdriver in one hand and was ordered to drop it. He didn't and was pepper-sprayed. He continued advancing on the officer still refusing commands to drop the screwdriver. He was shot twice when he raised his hand with the screwdriver.
A witness said shortly after his death it appeared to her Dumas only raised his hand to wipe pepper spray from his eyes.
It was later determined Dumas was not involved in the Elmwood home invasion.
Winnipeg Police Association president Loren Schinkel said the Ontario report backs up that earlier police investigation.
"This was a truly unfortunate situation. It has a lasting impact on everyone involved."

Dumas' sister, Jessica Paul, said she wasn't surprised the independent review absolved the officer of any criminal wrongdoing. Paul said now that the report is back, it opens the door for a provincial inquest to be held. An inquest is mandatory in Manitoba when someone dies as the result of a police act.
A date could not be set until the report from the Ontario Crown attorney was submitted.
"I'm really, really looking forward to it," Paul said. "We need to hear what happened. I'll maybe hear things I don't want to hear, but nothing could be as bad as the day we lost Matthew."
The case was first investigated by Winnipeg Police Service's homicide unit. Detectives determined nothing illegal occurred but sent their findings to Calgary police for a review.
The Calgary review also said no charges should be laid. The entire file was then sent to Ontario for a final legal evaluation.
The Dumas family filed a wrongful death claim against the police service last Jan. 29 in a bid to show Dumas' death was "caused by wrongful act, neglect or default."
The case remains before the courts.
